mentl/f7a331c:
STAGE 4. SYNTAX §«Type aliases» gives `type NonEmpty = [a] where len(self) > 0`
as THE refined-alias form, and the parser its own spec binds did not accept it:
parse_type_decl read the base with ident_at(p2) and probed p2 + 1 for `where`, so
only a SINGLE-token base could be refined. `[Int]` is three tokens (`[ Int ]`), so
`where` sat at p2 + 3, unseen — P_UnexpectedToken on `where` at the `]`, and then
E_MissingVariable on the len/self left orphaned in the un-parsed predicate.

The fix parses the whole base type FIRST (parse_type_ty, which already handles
`[a]`, `Option(k)`, records), then branches on what FOLLOWS it: `where` refines,
`|`/`+`/`-`/`&` is a variant or named row, a constructor payload is a
single-variant ADT, nothing is a transparent alias. One read of the base serves
every case; the single-token probe and its dead `base_val` are gone.

The wheel declares no `[base] where` alias, so its own emit is unchanged and
m2 == m3 stayed byte-identical — but the parser fn's bytes DID change, which the
march's m2==m3 clean verdict does not surface (it re-pins only on m2 != m3). This
is the wheel-neutral-yet-tool-changing case: boot is the tool, so the fix is not
live until boot carries it. Re-pinned boot = m2 (ab34a853…, m2==m3 verified);
old boot failed the form in a pty, this boot exits 0.

Tooling improved WITH the medium, in the same change: the new capability lands
with its guard. tests/frontier/mn-refined-alias-nonatomic.mn declares the form,
type-checks the predicate, and runs (exit 3); a parser regression re-surfaces the
mismatches and fails run_program's diagnostic check. frontier 47 -> 50, board
whole, census 1233, m2 == m3.

mentl/f7bb317:
Six fixes that together make handler state variables work correctly inside
handler arm closures compiled to WASM. Before: the WASM-compiled checker
crashed reading source strings as type pointers because handler state
variables were UNRESOLVED in closure bodies. After: all crucibles pass,
the self-hosted checker runs in WASM with correct state propagation.

1. lowir_walk.lux — walk_ir recurses into LMakeClosure fn_def bodies.
   The walker was blind to closure bodies; any tree-walk transform
   (subst_state_to_cells, collect_free_lowir) stopped at LMakeClosure.
   Destructure LFn, walk the body list, reconstruct. Pure structural.

2. lower.lux — substitute handler record before storing. The old code
   called subst_state_to_cells on LIndex(record, i) which contained zero
   state variable names — always a no-op. Now substitute lowered_handler
   itself; closures inside get their "s" → "__hs_s_42" renames.

3. lower.lux — ResumeExpr lowers to stash-then-update-then-return. For
   indirect dispatch (handler arm closures), state updates were dropped
   entirely. Now: stash value with OLD state, apply updates, return stash.
   resume(TVar(n)) with n = n + 1 correctly sees the old n.

4. lower.lux — wrap handler + body lowering in is_state_var effect.
   Nested lambdas in handler arms call filter_real_captures which fires
   is_state_var to filter state names from closure captures. State vars
   stay as globals (mutable cells), not captured by value.

5. lower_closure.lux — collect_free handles TupleExpr, ListExpr, MatchExpr,
   ResumeExpr, HandleExpr with proper pattern/state bindings. Match arms
   add pattern-bound names to bound. HandleExpr adds state binding names
   so they don't propagate as outer-function captures.

6. wasm_emit.lux — double-emit pure func expressions for nested closure
   calls. The __call_ptr temp from 57cbe8e was clobbered when args
   contained nested closure calls (lex_from(skip_comment(pos+2), ...)).
   Computed func exprs are pure capture

The signature skill mechanic. Catching a returning boomerang within
PERFECT_CATCH_WINDOW_FRAMES (10) of recall starting empowers the catcher's

clob/f7388a9:
Adds the "critic of Head C" — a linear probe that predicts the absolute
error of the confidence head, |head.predict(h) - actual_nll|. Trained
against a FROZEN snapshot of Head C that refreshes every
`meta_refresh` steps (default 500), which is the standard target-network
fix for the self-signal feedback oscillation the Plan agent flagged.
Without the snapshot, meta and head parameters would couple and their
MSEs would co-drift; with it, the meta-critic tracks a stable target.

CoreModel gains an optional MetaCritic. decode_step's adaptive loop
now has two gates: Head C's novelty detector must still fire, AND the
MetaCritic's prediction must be below `meta_unreliable_threshold`. When
the meta gate trips, the extra iterations are SUPPRESSED rather than
taken — the intuition is that Head C's uncertainty signal is itself
unreliable at this hidden state, so acting on it would waste joules.
A meta_suppressed_counter parallels extra_steps_counter; callers drain
both via take_*() into the metrics window.

MetricsWindow gains a `meta_suppressed` field and its jsonl schema is
extended to match. The clob-metrics dashboard renders it alongside
extra_steps.

calibrate-confidence gains --meta-out and --meta-refresh flags. When
--meta-out is set, a MetaCritic is co-trained in lock-step with the
confidence head: meta.train_step is called *before* head.train_step
each sample so the target label comes from the head state as it was
at this step, not its next update. This is the clean training ordering
for target networks.

Ingest gains --meta-critic and --meta-unreliable-threshold flags to
load a trained MetaCritic and install it into the model.

Verified end-to-end on the same synth-small model + eval_corpus as
Phase B+C:
  - Meta co-training: Head MSE 29→13→6 across 3 epochs; Meta MSE
    22→3→0.5 (converging faster because it tracks a simpler signal).
    Target snapshot refreshed 15× across 4764 training steps.
  - Adaptive-only ingest: 396 total extra steps, 0 suppressed.
  - Ada
